Q1.stem: Which of the following groups contains ONLY SI base units?

Q2.stem: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 meters. Ignoring air resistance, approximately how long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m/s2)

Q3.stem: Two resistors of 6 ohms and 3 ohms are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

Q4.stem: When light passes from air into water (a denser medium), what happens to its speed and wavelength?

Q5.stem: What is the temperature in Kelvin when the Celsius temperature is -73 degrees C?

Q6.stem: According to Newton's third law, when you push against a wall with a force of 50 N, the wall pushes back on you with a force of:

Q7.stem: A sound wave has a frequency of 440 Hz and travels at 340 m/s in air. What is its wavelength?

Q8.stem: A solid object floats in water with 70% of its volume submerged. What is the density of the object? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m3)

Q9.stem: A 2 kg ball is thrown upward with an initial velocity of 10 m/s. What is its kinetic energy at the moment of release? (Ignore air resistance)

Q10.stem: A hydraulic press has a small piston with area 5 cm2 and a large piston with area 100 cm2. If a force of 20 N is applied to the small piston, what force is exerted by the large piston?

Q11.stem: Which type of electromagnetic radiation has the shortest wavelength?

Q12.stem: During β-minus decay, a neutron in the nucleus is converted into a proton and emits:
options: An α particle and a γ ray

Q13.stem: A crane lifts a 500 kg load vertically by 10 meters in 25 seconds. What is the power output of the crane? (g = 10 m/s2)

Q14.stem: A 1000 kg car traveling at 20 m/s collides head-on with a stationary 2000 kg truck. If they stick together after the collision, what is their common velocity immediately after impact?

Q15.stem: A charged particle moving through a uniform magnetic field experiences a force. In which direction is this magnetic force relative to the particle's velocity?
options: Perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field
At a 45-degree angle to the velocity

Q16.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s over a distance of 200 m. What is the acceleration?

Q17.stem: An ambulance siren sounds at 800 Hz. As it approaches you at high speed, you perceive a frequency that is:

Q18.stem: A converging (convex) lens has a focal length of 10 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. Where does the image form?
options: 7.5 cm on the same side as the object

Q19.stem: A 12V battery is connected to a 4Ω resistor. What is the current flowing through the circuit?

Q20.stem: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 6 hours. If you start with 80 g, how much remains after 18 hours?

Q21.stem: In a CT scanner, the X-ray tube rotates around the patient and produces images at multiple angles. If the tube completes one full rotation in 0.5 s and the detector array has 1000 elements, approximately how many projections per second does the system acquire?

Q22.stem: An MRI machine operates at a magnetic field strength of 3.0 T. The gyromagnetic ratio of hydrogen protons is 42.58 MHz/T. What is the Larmor precession frequency of hydrogen nuclei in this scanner?

Q23.stem: Ultrasound waves travel through soft tissue at approximately 1540 m/s. If an echo returns 26 microseconds after the pulse was emitted, what is the depth of the reflecting structure?

Q24.stem: In radiation therapy, a patient receives a prescribed dose of 2 Gy to a tumor. If the tumor mass is 0.5 kg, how much energy is deposited in the tumor?

Q25.stem: An X-ray tube operates at a potential difference of 80 kV. What is the minimum wavelength (cutoff wavelength) of the X-rays produced? (h = 6.63 x 10-34 J-s, c = 3 x 108 m/s, e = 1.6 x 10-19 C)

Q26.stem: A diagnostic ultrasound transducer operates at 5 MHz. What is the approximate wavelength in soft tissue (speed of sound = 1540 m/s)?

Q27.stem: In MRI, the T1 relaxation time of a tissue is 800 ms. After an initial 90-degree RF pulse, what fraction of the longitudinal magnetization has recovered after 1600 ms?

Q28.stem: A cobalt-60 source used in radiation therapy has a half-life of 5.27 years. If the initial activity is 400 TBq, what will the activity be after approximately 10.54 years?

Q29.stem: A straight wire carries a current of 10 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance of 5 cm from the wire? (μ0 = 4π x 10-7 T-m/A)

Q30.stem: A proton (mass = 1.67 x 10-27 kg, charge = 1.6 x 10-19 C) moves at 2 x 106 m/s perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the radius of its circular path?

Q31.stem: A rectangular coil of 50 turns with dimensions 20 cm x 10 cm rotates in a uniform magnetic field of 0.4 T at 60 revolutions per second. What is the peak EMF generated?

Q32.stem: An electron enters a region where both an electric field E = 3000 V/m and a magnetic field B = 0.01 T are perpendicular to each other and to the electron's velocity. For the electron to pass through undeflected, what must its velocity be?

Q33.stem: A solenoid has 2000 turns per meter and carries a current of 3 A. What is the magnetic field inside the solenoid? (μ0 = 4π x 10-7 T-m/A)

Q34.stem: A circular loop of wire with radius 8 cm is placed in a magnetic field that increases uniformly from 0.2 T to 0.8 T in 0.3 s. What is the magnitude of the induced EMF in the loop?

Q35.stem: Two parallel wires separated by 10 cm each carry a current of 5 A in opposite directions. What is the force per meter between the wires, and is it attractive or repulsive?

Q36.stem: A transformer has 500 turns on the primary coil and 50 turns on the secondary coil. If the input voltage is 220 V AC, what is the output voltage?

Q37.stem: Light with a wavelength of 400 nm strikes a metal surface with a work function of 2.0 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons? (h = 6.63 x 10-34 J-s, c = 3 x 108 m/s, 1 eV = 1.6 x 10-19 J)

Q38.stem: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron (mass = 9.11 x 10-31 kg) accelerated through a potential difference of 100 V? (h = 6.63 x 10-34 J-s, e = 1.6 x 10-19 C)

Q39.stem: In the Compton effect, an X-ray photon with wavelength 0.071 nm scatters off an electron at an angle of 90 degrees. What is the wavelength shift? (Compton wavelength of electron = 0.00243 nm)

Q40.stem: An atom makes a transition from an energy level at -1.5 eV to one at -3.4 eV. What is the wavelength of the emitted photon? (h = 6.63 x 10-34 J-s, c = 3 x 108 m/s, 1 eV = 1.6 x 10-19 J)

Q41.stem: According to the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, if the position of an electron is measured with an uncertainty of 0.1 nm, what is the minimum uncertainty in its momentum? (h-bar = 1.055 x 10-34 J-s)

Q42.stem: The threshold frequency for a photoemissive surface is 5.0 x 1014 Hz. What is the work function of the material in electron volts? (h = 6.63 x 10-34 J-s, 1 eV = 1.6 x 10-19 J)

Q43.stem: Blood flows through an artery of radius 4 mm at a velocity of 0.3 m/s. If the artery narrows to a radius of 2 mm due to plaque buildup, what is the velocity of blood in the narrowed section? (Assume incompressible flow.)

Q44.stem: Water flows through a horizontal pipe that narrows from a cross-section of 40 cm2 to 10 cm2. If the pressure in the wider section is 200 kPa and the flow speed there is 2 m/s, what is the pressure in the narrow section? (Density of water = 1000 kg/m3)

Q45.stem: A fluid with viscosity 0.004 Pa-s flows through a tube of radius 3 mm and length 0.5 m under a pressure difference of 800 Pa. What is the volume flow rate according to Poiseuille's law?

Q46.stem: A steel ball of density 7800 kg/m3 and radius 1 mm falls through glycerin (density 1260 kg/m3, viscosity 1.5 Pa-s). What is the terminal velocity of the ball? (g = 10 m/s2)

Q47.stem: The Reynolds number for blood flow in the aorta is approximately 2000. If the aorta has a diameter of 2.5 cm, blood density is 1060 kg/m3 and viscosity is 3.5 x 10-3 Pa-s, what is the average flow velocity?

Q48.stem: A manometer connected to a patient's artery reads a gauge pressure of 120 mmHg. What is this pressure in pascals? (Density of mercury = 13600 kg/m3, g = 10 m/s2)

Q49.stem: A Carnot engine operates between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. What is the efficiency of this engine?

Q50.stem: During an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas at 400 K, the volume doubles. If the gas contains 2 moles, how much work does the gas do? (R = 8.314 J/(mol-K), ln 2 = 0.693)

Q51.stem: The entropy change when 1 kg of water at 100 degrees C is converted entirely to steam at 100 degrees C and 1 atm is closest to which value? (Lv = 2260 kJ/kg)

Q52.stem: An ideal gas undergoes an adiabatic process where the volume is compressed to 1/8 of its original volume. If the initial temperature is 300 K and γ = 5/3 (monatomic gas), what is the final temperature?

Q53.stem: At the triple point of water (273.16 K, 611.73 Pa), which statement is correct?
options: Only ice and liquid water coexist in equilibrium
Only liquid water and water vapor coexist in equilibrium
Ice, liquid water, and water vapor coexist in equilibrium
Water can only exist as a liquid at the triple point

Q54.stem: A converging lens with a focal length of 20 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. What is the image distance and magnification?

Q55.stem: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 40 cm. An object is placed 15 cm from the mirror. Where is the image formed?
options: 60 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror

Q56.stem: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +10 cm and -15 cm are placed in contact. What is the focal length of the combination?

Q57.stem: A microscope has an objective lens with focal length 5 mm and an eyepiece with focal length 25 mm. If the tube length (distance between lenses) is 160 mm, what is the total magnification for a near point of 250 mm?

Q58.stem: A ray of light enters a glass slab (refractive index 1.5) from air at an angle of incidence of 30 degrees. What is the angle of refraction inside the glass?

Q59.stem: The critical angle for total internal reflection at a glass-air interface is 42 degrees. What is the refractive index of the glass?

Q60.stem: Which of the following is a base SI unit?
